items.title: Hint use of `uv run` if `uvx` is given a script path
items.reason: This tracks the intended handling of actual `.py` script paths. The new report differs because its input is a supported Git requirement, not a script path.

items.title: Return error when running uvx with a .py script
items.reason: This implemented the extension-only early checks for direct targets and `--from`, confirming the false-positive mechanism. It did not address Git URLs ending in `.py`.

items.title: feature: uvx for github repos
items.reason: This establishes that Git repository requirements are supported through `--from` and direct invocation. It does not cover the `.py` suffix collision.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using the exact error, sample repository, `.py` endings, direct and `--from` Git requirements, script-path handling, and PEP 508/tool-request terminology. astral-sh/uv#6296 and astral-sh/uv#11337 concern older general requirement parsing. astral-sh/uv#12713, astral-sh/uv#15882, and astral-sh/uv#16303 fail later during Git handling and were ruled out.

type_reason: Current source intercepts both the direct target and `--from` value with an extension-only script-path check before parsing the tool requirement. A Git URL ending in `.py` therefore reaches `PackageName::from_str` and is incorrectly rejected. No existing issue or pull request tracks this false positive.
summary: No existing report tracks the same `.py` Git-URL false positive. The closest history is the local-script safeguard in astral-sh/uv#10784 and astral-sh/uv#11623; astral-sh/uv#8199 confirms Git repository tool requests are supported.
draft_response: Thanks for the report. Git requirements are supported in both forms shown, but the current `.py` script-path check runs before the tool requirement is parsed. A Git URL whose repository name ends in `.py` is therefore incorrectly treated as a script path and validated as a package name. This is distinct from astral-sh/uv#10784, which handles actual `.py` script paths. The next step is to narrow that check and add coverage for both the direct and `--from` forms.
